doc.title: Steve Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 25, 2002

chapter: Richmond and arriving in New York
title: Jam sessions at the Blue Note, Augie's and Bruce Barth's house
summary: Where late 1980s jam sessions happened and who attended; he met Bruce Barth and started playing at his house.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: What kind of places did those jam sessions happen in back then? Were they small clubs and that kind of thing?

Let’s see, well the late 1980s we’re talking like the Blue Note had a late night jam session, like after the last show during the week and so usually starting at 1:00. And people like Justin Robertson and the Harper Brothers were heading those jam sessions. Then there was a jam session uptown at this place called Augie’s, which is now called Smoke. But Augie’s was a place where a lot of guys honed their craft, guys like Larry Goldings and Freddy Bryant, a young guitarist I’ve been working with for quite a while, © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-
Billy Drummond, a lot of the young musicians would just go up and play all the time. The Village — not the Village Vanguard but the other club—

The Village Gate had some stuff going. Then they had another club uptown near Columbia University that also had some sessions, and of course my good friend and partner Bruce Barth, we met around that time and started jamming together at his house. And his wife was kind enough to let us all come over a couple of times a week and play. And we’ve been working together now for like fourteen years as a result of that. So yeah it happened in a variety of clubs.
